problem_type: Agent failure evidence loses provider/lifecycle classification
symptom: A real Agent turn can stream assistant text and then render only the generic 发送失败 message, leaving the vertical runner unable to distinguish a provider auth/quota/network failure from an Agent lifecycle failure without inspecting unsafe raw diagnostics.
direct_cause: ProjectAgentResidentShell rendered failure items with localized text and kept item.code/item.message only inside the renderer branch; no stable DOM field exposed a bounded error code or category for truthful journey evidence.
class_root: The Agent failure projection had no redacted diagnostic boundary between Host/provider error facts and UI automation evidence, so runners either guessed from a generic message or would need to expose raw provider text that could contain credentials.
affected_population: Users seeing a failed Agent turn after partial assistant output
Real M0-M5 journey diagnostics that must classify provider and lifecycle failures
Any UI automation consuming Agent failure state without access to a Host snapshot
internal_only_reason: The diagnostic attributes are an internal Nomi Host-to-renderer evidence contract and must not expose provider payloads or credentials.
invariants: Failure articles expose only a bounded allowlisted code and one of auth, quota, network, provider, lifecycle, capability, or unknown categories.
Raw failure messages and provider response bodies are never copied into diagnostic DOM attributes or runner evidence.
A journey runner does not retry an unknown failure until structured evidence establishes that retry is safe and expected.
generality_proof: All Agent failure items render through the single items.map failure article in ProjectAgentResidentShell, so the same safe code/category projection covers provider, Host lifecycle, and capability failures across creation, storyboard, generation, and preview surfaces.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Project internal failure facts into bounded diagnostic attributes while retaining localized user-facing copy.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The runner consumes only the bounded data-agent-error-code and data-agent-error-message-category fields.
User-facing failure copy remains localized and does not become a raw provider diagnostic.

recurrence.reason: Every provider or Host failure can otherwise collapse to the same generic sendFailed copy, making truthful retry and failure classification impossible.
same_class_scan: Searched ProjectAgentResidentShell, projectAgentClient, workbenchAgentRunner, runtimeVendorError, and failure-card projections for provider/lifecycle diagnostics.
Confirmed the Host already classifies runtime facts internally; this slice exposes only a redacted renderer evidence projection.

prevention.invariant: No raw provider error message or credential-shaped value is placed in Agent diagnostic attributes.
prevention.failure_mode: Unknown or malformed codes map to unknown; category classification is a closed allowlist and the runner remains fail-closed.
prevention.strategy: Normalize code with a strict identifier regex and derive a bounded category from internal code/message text before rendering.

legacy_paths.rationale: The existing localized failure card remains the user-facing path; this adds bounded evidence attributes without a parallel renderer.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency is introduced; classification uses existing Host error facts.

migration: No persisted data migration is needed; attributes are ephemeral DOM evidence.
residual_risks: If the Host supplies only a generic runtime_error with no transport facts, the category remains provider or unknown and the runner must stay blocked.
The DOM projection cannot replace a full Host snapshot when deeper correlation is required; it only supplies safe first-line evidence.
